summary_text: In March 2026, four independent orders were placed across weekdays and weekends. The month featured distinct, non-recurring shopping events: a festival-related basket (Holi Color, Sweets Mithai) in early March, and separate single-category purchases of Vegetables, Milk, and Sunflower Oil later in the month. No daypart, category combination, or product behavior repeated across independent dates; therefore, no stable patterns or routines are established.

trend_claims.claim_text: A single order on 2026-03-02 (weekday, morning) combined Holi Color and Sweets Mithai, compatible with Holi festival preparations.
A single order on 2026-03-17 (weekday, evening) contained only Vegetables (6 distinct items, quantity 7), suggesting a need for fresh ingredients.
A single order on 2026-03-22 (weekend, evening) contained only Milk (5 units), suggesting a need for dairy.
A single order on 2026-03-26 (weekday, morning) contained only Sunflower Oil, suggesting a need for cooking oil.

shopping_need_text: The user demonstrated needs for festival-specific items (Holi Color, Sweets Mithai), fresh produce (Vegetables), dairy (Milk), and cooking staples (Sunflower Oil) across four separate, non-repeating transactions.
uncertainty_text: All observed behaviors are based on single, independent dates. No repetition exists to establish durable preferences, routines, or stable category associations. Confidence in any inferred user behavior is low.
